eip.detail_20_: Description of the enhanced 95 billing mode:
eip.detail_21_:
1. Bill cycle
Bills are generated for each calendar month.
2. Billing formula
Monthly peak bandwidth x Monthly peak bandwidth price x Shared bandwidth in-use days/Calendar days of a month.
3. Monthly peak bandwidth price
The price is preset and has nothing to do with the number of days contained in a month.
4. Shared bandwidth in-use days
Calculated based on the actual duration when the shared bandwidth is used. For example, if you apply for a shared bandwidth at 12: 00, the shared bandwidth use time is half a day. Shared bandwidth in-use days = Number of collected bandwidth values in a month/288.
5. Monthly peak bandwidth
The monthly peak bandwidth is calculated based on the enhanced 95 billing mode and has some peak bandwidth values discarded. It must be higher than the monthly baseline bandwidth.
6. Daily baseline bandwidth
Daily baseline bandwidth = Baseline percentage x Shared bandwidth. The baseline percentage is 20%. (In enhanced 95 billing mode, the shared bandwidth can be adjusted in real time, and the adjustment takes effect immediately. After the shared bandwidth is adjusted, the baseline bandwidth changes accordingly.) The daily baseline bandwidth is calculated based on the maximum baseline bandwidth set for a day. For example, if the bandwidth is adjusted from 100 Mbit/s to 300 Mbit/s and then to 200 Mbit/s during a day, the daily baseline bandwidth is 60 Mbit/s (300 x 20%).
7. Monthly baseline bandwidth
The bandwidth may be adjusted frequently to suit the traffic requirements during a month. The monthly baseline bandwidth is calculated based on the following formula (only the integer is retained in the calculated result):Monthly baseline bandwidth = (Baseline bandwidth 1 x Number of days using baseline bandwidth 1 + Baseline bandwidth 2 x Number of days using baseline bandwidth 2 + ... + Baseline bandwidth n x Number of days using baseline bandwidth n)/Number of days using all baseline bandwidths in a month.
8. Monthly peak bandwidth calculation method
Inbound and outbound traffic data is collected every five minutes. The averages of both inbound bandwidth and outbound bandwidth within five minutes are calculated, and the larger one is used as the bandwidth for that collection. After all meter readings within a day are obtained, they are sequenced in descending order. The top four peak bandwidth values are discarded, and the fifth peak bandwidth value is used as the daily peak bandwidth. If less than five peak bandwidth values are obtained on a day, the last one in the peak bandwidth sequence is used as the daily peak bandwidth. The daily peak bandwidth is an integer (the decimal is discarded).
At the end of each month, the daily peak bandwidth values are sequenced in descending order. The average of the top five daily peak bandwidth values is the monthly peak bandwidth (retain only the integer). If less than five daily peak bandwidth values are obtained, the average of all the daily peak bandwidth values in the month is the monthly peak bandwidth. If the baseline bandwidth of a month is greater than the average of the daily peak bandwidth values, the monthly peak bandwidth is equal to the baseline bandwidth of the month. Otherwise, the monthly peak bandwidth is equal to the average of daily peak bandwidth values.

1. Log read and write traffic: The read and write traffic is calculated based on the size of the transmission traffic after compression. Typically, the maximum compression ratio is 5:1.
Example: If the original log file size is 10 GB and the compressed file size is 2 GB, you will be billed for 2 GB.

2. Log index traffic: By default, full-text indexes are created for original logs, and you will be billed for the traffic when logs are written.
Example: The original log file size is 10 GB and the traffic used for index creation is 10 GB, so you need to pay 0.8 USD.
lts.detail_14_:
3. Log storage: Fees are calculated by size of raw logs (including backups; compressed). Storage has two tiers: standard and cold.
Example: ① Daily standard storage fee for 10 GB of raw logs: $0.000125 USD x 24h x 10 GB = $0.03 USD ② Daily cold storage fee for 10 GB of raw logs: $0.00003993 USD x 24h x 10 GB = $0.01 USD.
lts.detail_16_:
1. Free quota
In this example, 80 MB of logs are added every day, and all logs are stored for 7 days.
Daily read and write traffic: 80 MB/5 (compression rate) = 16 MB. Accumulated read and write traffic for 30 days: 16 MB x 30 = 480 MB (within the 500 MB free quota).
Accumulated index traffic for 30 days: 80 MB x 30 = 2,400 MB. 30-day index fee: (2,400 MB – 500 MB)/1,024 x $0.08 USD/GB = $0.15 USD.
Log storage space: 80 MB/day x 7 days = 560 MB. 30-day storage fee: (560 MB – 500 MB)/1,024 x $0.000125 USD/hour/GB x 24 hours x 30 days = $0.01 USD.
lts.detail_17_:
2. Excess quota
Assume that 100 GB of new logs is generated every day, the standard storage duration is set to 30 days, and the cold storage duration is set to 7 days.
Log read/write traffic: Daily read and write traffic after compression = 100 GB/5 (compression rate) = 20 GB. 30-day accumulated read and write traffic = 20 GB x 30 days = 600 GB. 30-day read and write fee = (600 GB – 500 MB/1,024) x $0.05 USD = $29.98 USD.
Log index traffic: Index traffic = 100 GB x 30 days = 3,000 GB. 30-day index fee: (3,000 GB – 500 MB/1,024) x $0.08 USD= $239.96 USD.
Standard storage fee: Log volume = 100 GB/day x 30 days = 3,000 GB. 30-day storage fee = (3,000 GB – 500 MB/1,024) x $0.000125 USD x 24h x 30 days = $269.96 USD.
Cold storage fee: Log volume = 100 GB/day x 7 days = 700 GB. 30-day storage fee = 700 GB x $0.00003993 USD x 24h x 30 days = $20.12 USD.
